question: An engineer asks your developer productivity agent to add a distributed lock to a legacy batch scheduler, so that two servers never run the same job at once. The engineer has never built a distributed lock before. Before any code is written, the engineer tells the agent to use the interview pattern. Which questions from the agent best serve the purpose of this pattern?

options.text: The agent asks what must happen when a server crashes while it still holds the lock, and how long a lock may stay held before it expires.
options.reason: In an unfamiliar domain, the interview pattern has Claude ask about design considerations the developer may not have anticipated, such as failure modes, before implementing.

options.text: The agent asks which file names, code formatting rules, and comment style the engineer prefers for the new lock module in the scheduler.
options.reason: These are routine style preferences, not design considerations such as failure modes, so they do not surface what the engineer failed to anticipate.

options.text: The agent asks the engineer to restate the requirement that two servers must never run the same job at once, and then confirms that it understood.
options.reason: The engineer already stated this requirement, so repeating it surfaces no unanticipated consideration, and surfacing those is the purpose of the interview pattern.

options.text: The agent asks whether it may read the scheduler files with the Read tool and run commands with the Bash tool before it edits code.
options.reason: Tool permissions are not design considerations of the solution, so these questions surface no failure modes or other points the engineer did not anticipate.
